The deadly attack followed an earlier strike that damaged the enterprise without causing casualties, while overnight Russian attacks elsewhere in the Dnipropetrovsk region injured eight people.

Ukraine Hits Russian Oil, Port Infrastructure in Strikes Stretching From Arctic to Caspian — President Volodymyr Zelensky said Ukrainian forces struck eight Russian infrastructure sites supporting Moscow’s war in a single day. The attacks stretched from an oil refinery in the Arctic Yamalo-Nenets region to the Makhachkala port on the Caspian Sea, which Ukraine says Russia used to import Iranian Shahed drones.

Kyiv Shortens Curfew, Changes Metro Rules as Russian Drone Attacks Intensify — Kyiv has shortened its curfew and introduced tighter rules for public transport, bridges and public events as Russia steps up drone attacks on the capital. The new measures include changes to metro operations during air alerts and special transport arrangements for passengers caught out by the curfew.

Ukraine Names New Leaders of Donetsk Military Groups — Ukraine has named two revamped military groupings within the Donetsk region where Brig. Gen. Biletsky will lead Center, and Brig. Gen. Prokopenko is expected to head Azov.

FSB Accuses Kyiv of Planning Attack on British Ambassador to Moscow — Russia’s FSB published a video of the interrogation of a Russian citizen who worked as a security officer at the British Embassy in Moscow. In it, he appears to confess that he had passed intelligence to a Ukrainian handler intended to be used in an attack on the ambassador.

SBU Unit Chief Detained Over Ammunition Storage Violations After 35 Killed Near Kyiv — The head of a Ukrainian Security Service unit has been placed in custody over alleged ammunition storage violations in Mila, Kyiv region. A Russian drone strike on the site on Aug. 28 triggered explosions that killed 35 people, injured 21, and left one person missing.

Russian Drone Strikes State-Owned Ukrnafta Gas Station in Kyiv, Smoke Seen Over City — A Russian drone fell onto a gas station in Kyiv’s Holosiivskyi district on Thursday, Sept. 10, sparking a fire and setting one car ablaze. Mayor Vitalii Klitschko said three people were injured and receiving medical treatment.

Xi Jinping’s September of Summits — While China seeks to maintain its role as the leading economic partner and strategic competitor for the US, the program of meetings planned by Beijing in September indicate Xi Jinping’s push to act within a multipolar world.

How ‘Call Centers’ Helped Bring Down Ukraine’s Prosecutor General — Kyiv Post takes a detailed look at the NABU "Carthage" operation. We explain what lies behind Prosecutor General Kravchenko’s resignation, and why it is connected to sinister call centers whose activities have been felt globally.

3,200 km Into Russia: Ukraine Hits 2 Major Gas Facilities in Record-Breaking Strike — Ukraine’s SSO said they struck the Novy Urengoy and Purovsky gas-condensate plants in Russia’s Yamalo-Nenets region. The drones traveled more than 3,000 kilometers, marking what Ukraine called its deepest strike of the war.

Polish FM Sees Little Hope for Ukraine Peace Talks as Putin Holds Out — Polish Foreign Minister Radosław Sikorski expressed little optimism about Ukraine peace talks, saying Russia continues to reject ceasefire proposals and pursue its existing goals. He urged stronger support for Ukraine’s military capabilities, while warning that Poland and Latvia face growing Russian hybrid threats, including airspace violations, migration pressure and sabotage.

Ukraine’s International Reserves Fall 5% to $48.7 Billion in August — Ukraine's international reserves dropped slightly to $48.7 billion in August. Despite heavy central bank interventions to stabilize the hryvnia, current reserves remain sufficient to cover four months of future national imports. Ukraine also received the USL loan tranche.

Ousted Defense Minister Fedorov Says Ukraine to Create Largest Defense Tech Fund — Ousted Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov says Ukraine will soon launch its largest Defense Tech venture fund. The initiative will back military startups developing battlefield robotics, air-defense interceptors and low-cost missiles.

Zelensky Arrives in Canada for Three-Day Visit Focused on Defense, Energy — Zelensky arrived in Canada for a three-day visit focused on boosting defense, economic and energy cooperation. Talks are expected to include ballistic missile defense, a key vulnerability for Ukraine as Russia continues its long-range missile and drone attacks.
ISW Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment, September 9, 2026 — War in Ukraine - Latest update, key takeaways and map from the Institute for the Study of War on September 9, 2026.

Massive Russian Drone Assault Hits 5 Locations in Kryvyi Rih, Injuring 5 — Five people were injured in an overnight Russian drone attack on Kryvyi Rih. Two were hospitalized, including a 42-year-old man in serious condition.

Zelensky’s Drone-Disrupted Flight Highlights Wartime Travel Risks as Kyiv Calls Near-Miss Claims Exaggerated — A Russian drone incursion delayed Zelensky’s departure from Moldova, highlighting the security risks surrounding his extensive wartime travel and the sharp contrast with Putin’s much more limited foreign trips.

Russian Drone Strike on Sumy Shopping Center Kills 2, Injures at Least 20 — A Russian drone struck Sumy’s Manufaktura shopping center, killing a 21-year-old man and woman and injuring at least 20 people, including three teenagers.

Kim Jong Un Publicly Praises North Korean Troops Fighting for Russia — Kim Jong Un praised troops serving in “overseas military operations” during North Korea’s founding anniversary, publicly normalizing a deployment that has sent an estimated 14,000 to 15,000 soldiers to support Russia’s war against Ukraine.

PACE Panel Backs Using €260B in Russian Assets for Ukraine’s Legal Claims — PACE lawmakers have backed a proposal to use frozen Russian Central Bank assets to fund potentially billions in compensation for Ukraine under Strasbourg Court rulings.

Italian Deputy PM Tajani Urges Zelensky to Include Italy, Poland in Peace Talks — Italian Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs, Antonio Tajani, urged President Volodymyr Zelensky to involve Italy and Poland in future peace initiatives, alongside France and Germany. Zelensky separately said Europe will take part in all future negotiating formats because the outcome affects the continent’s wider security.

Zelensky’s Plane Faced Drone Attack in Moldova – Norwegian PM — Norwegian Prime Minister Gahr Støre told the state media channel NRK that the aircraft carrying President Zelensky was almost hit by a drone during take-off in Moldova en-route to the funeral of the late Norwegian King Harald in Oslo on Tuesday Sept. 8.

Russia Signs Strategic Oil Reserve Deal With Vietnam — Russia signed a framework agreement to cooperate on creating a strategic oil reserve in Vietnam during President Tô Lâm’s visit to Moscow on Wednesday, Sept. 9. The countries also adopted a 50-point partnership statement, discussed visa-free travel, and launched a joint infectious disease research laboratory.

CIA Director Ratcliffe Could Take Larger Role in Ukraine Peace Talks — As Russian President Vladimir Putin hardens his demands in peace negotiations, sources say CIA Director John Ratcliffe is being prepared for a larger role in US led talks with Russia and Ukraine. The possible shift, sources told the Financial Times, could reduce the roles of US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner. The White House rejected the report as false, calling it “totally fake news” on Wednesday, Sept. 9.
Ex-CIA Chief: NATO Is Weak and the Baltics Are Next — Former CIA Chief of Station Sean Wiswesser says NATO’s deterrence is too weak and warns that the Baltic states could be Russia’s next target.

Kyiv Under Air Alert for Over 6 Hours as Russian Attack Kills 1, Injures 16 — A Russian drone attack on Kyiv killed a 67-year-old woman and injured 16 people on Wednesday, Sept. 9. The city was under an air-raid alert for more than six hours as drones struck residential areas and damaged civilian infrastructure. The barrage came after US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner left Kyiv, following weekend meetings with President Volodymyr Zelensky in the capital and Russian President Vladimir Put

Zelensky, Norway's PM Støre Meet Defense Companies Over FREYJA Air Shield — President Volodymyr Zelensky and Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre met defense industry leaders in Oslo to advance the FREYJA anti-ballistic program on Wednesday, Sept. 9. The meeting comes as Ukraine continues its winter preparations and with Russia expected to intensify its attacks on the country’s critical infrastructure, including power grids and water supplies.

Fear of Backdoor Mobilization Grows in Russia — Increasing numbers of Russians who have been summoned to military enlistment offices supposedly to verify and update their registration details have found orders inserted into their military ID cards which commits them to reporting to a collection point if mobilization is declared.

Fintech Firm Activitis Emerges as Bidder for WOG Owners’ Bizbank — WOG fuel network owners are preparing to sell Bizbank, considering the commercial lender a secondary asset. FinTech company Activitis has emerged as the potential buyer. While antimonopoly clearance is secured, finalizing the deal requires central bank approval and several months.

Russian Drone Hits Kyiv Apartment Block, Kills Woman — A Russian drone struck a nine-story residential building in Kyiv’s Dniprovskyi district, causing a fire and killing a woman, city authorities said. One other person was injured in the latest attack, with at least nine people already wounded during earlier Russian strikes across the capital on Wednesday.

Russian Sabotage Ops in Europe — Facing battlefield stagnation, Russia has escalated sabotage operations across Europe – explosions, drone incidents, and infrastructure disruptions – aiming to raise the cost of supporting Ukraine and erode public backing. The recent Leipzig airport attack marks a turning point, with Germany directly attributing it to Moscow. Expect intensified European counter-intelligence efforts and possible tit-for-tat responses, while Russia may shift toward disruptive or ma

Ukraine Presents Domestically Developed Pegas IFV — Weighing 35 tons, Ukraine’s newly unveiled Pegas infantry fighting vehicle (IFV) is said to meet Level 6 of NATO’s STANAG 4569 protection standard, with a maximum speed of 70 kilometers per hour (43 mph) and an operational range of 500 kilometers (310 miles).

Trump, Putin and Xi Could Meet in November, Peskov Says — The Kremlin says Trump, Putin, and Xi could meet at the APEC summit in China in November. Peskov also said Moscow expects trilateral Ukraine talks to resume soon and remains engaged in prisoner-exchange discussions.

Kremlin War Drone Flies 30 Minutes Over Romania Unimpeded by NATO — A Russian jet-powered Shahed penetrated at least 50 km into Romanian airspace on Sept. 8 and evaded two scrambled F-18s. It returned to Moldova and crashed as NATO conducted an unusually large Black Sea air surveillance exercise.

Drone Nets Appear on Roads Near Chornobyl — Anti-drone nets have appeared over roads leading toward Chornobyl as Ukraine strengthens approaches near the Belarusian border. The barriers are designed to protect vehicles and pedestrians from FPV drones by trapping them or causing their explosives to detonate before reaching a target.

Russia Replaces Polish Memorial With ‘Special Military Operation’ Statues — Russia’s Yakutia has unveiled a new monument dedicated to two soldiers who died fighting in Russia’s invasion of Ukraine, with one having served in the 155th Marine Brigade accused of murdering civilians in Bucha. The monument is located where a memorial dedicated to exiled Poles and Lithuanians in the 19th century once stood.

Russian Strikes Could Add Up to 0.6 Points to Ukraine’s Inflation, NBU Says — Russian strikes on warehouses, logistics hubs, and energy infrastructure are no longer just an inflation risk for Ukraine – they are showing up in the data, NBU Deputy Governor Volodymyr Lepushynskyi wrote in an op-ed. He estimates that rebuilding logistics networks could add 0.4-0.6 percentage points to annual inflation by the end of 2026, even as businesses adapt by rerouting supply chains and restoring damaged capac

71% of Ukrainians Say They Are Happy Despite Russia’s War, Poll Shows — A KIIS survey found that 71% of Ukrainians living in government-controlled territory consider themselves happy, up from 58% in December 2024. Sixteen percent said they were unhappy.

What Did US Envoys Achieve in Moscow and Kyiv? — US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner held talks with Vladimir Putin and Volodymyr Zelensky to explore ending the war. While Moscow called the discussions constructive, commentators remain divided: some see diplomacy as progress, while others argue Putin is stalling or seeking unacceptable concessions. Ukrainian voices stress that Russia’s demands threaten Ukraine’s sovereignty and statehood.

Russian Shahed Hits Kharkiv–Izyum Train, Injuring 7 and Sparking Fire at Station — A Russian Shahed drone struck a Kharkiv-Izyum passenger train near Iskra on Sept. 9, injuring 7 people and sparking a fire. The attack follows several recent strikes on Ukraine’s passenger trains and railway infrastructure.

Russia Suspends Flights 1,800km From Ukraine as Drones Threaten Siberian Oil-Producing Heartland — Russia has imposed flight restrictions in the Khanty-Mansi Autonomous Okrug, over 1,800 km (1,118 miles) from Ukraine, due to drone threats. The region is also home to 40% of Russia’s crude production, and the threats suggest a shift in how Kyiv is hitting Moscow where it hurts.

Ukraine Says It Hit Russian Missile Carrier Admiral Essen in Novorossiysk Strike — On the night of Sept. 8-9, Ukrainian drones attacked the port of Novorossiysk and nearby military sites, with Ukraine claiming to have struck the oil terminal and to have destroyed naval vessels, aircraft and air defense radars located in the area. Reports from Russian authorities claim that debris from intercepted drones struck a church, industrial sites and residential buildings, killing four people and injuring

Abramovich Loses Third Bid to Escape EU Sanctions — The EU General Court rejected his challenge to the latest extension of restrictions imposed over Russia’s invasion of Ukraine, as well as his demand for compensation. Abramovich remains subject to an EU asset freeze and travel ban.

Kyiv Warns Russia Will ‘Test’ New Long-Range Missile Against Western Ukraine — Russia plans to complete testing of an unnamed ballistic missile with a range of up to 800 kilometers by the end of 2026, according to Ukraine’s military intelligence directorate. The agency added that Moscow is seeking to both expand missile production and intensify mobilization after monthly battlefield losses exceeded recruitment in August.

German FM Urges Ukrainian Men to Return Home — German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul said Ukrainian men of military age living in Germany should return to Ukraine, however stressing that they must not be forced to do so. He offered Berlin’s help in identifying and contacting them through residency, registration, and social-benefit records.

Russia Strikes Border Crossing With Moldova, Killing 2 and Injuring 3 — Russian drones struck the Starokozache border crossing with Moldova in Odesa region, killing two civilians and injuring three. The crossing was temporarily closed, while 16 people were evacuated from the area.

Russia Wants Postwar Ukraine Turned Into ‘Buffer Zone,’ Lavrov Says — Lavrov says Russia wants Ukraine transformed into a giant “buffer zone” after the war, rejecting any postwar settlement that leaves Kyiv’s current government in place. His remarks come as US President Donald Trump’s envoys push to revive peace talks, amid the widening gap between Washington’s diplomacy and Moscow’s demands.

From Trenches to Catwalk: Ukraine’s Amputee Soldiers Hit the Runway — Ukrainian war veterans took to the runway at Kyiv Fashion Week, turning prosthetics into a statement of style, resilience and inclusion. For amputees who lost limbs fighting Russia, the show offered a rare chance to move from destruction to creation – and to reclaim confidence in public.

Russian Drone Slams Into Kyiv High-Rise, Injuring 4 — A Russian jet-powered drone struck a 24-story residential building in Kyiv early Sept. 9, injuring four people and sparking a fire. The attack came amid a wider overnight drone assault on Kyiv Oblast, as Germany pledged urgent deliveries of Patriot interceptor missiles to Ukraine.

Ukraine Unveils New Air Defense Missile to Replace Soviet Osa-AKM Stocks — Ukraine has unveiled the RK-19, a new air defense missile designed to replace dwindling Soviet-era 9M33 stocks for its Osa-AKM systems. Displayed at Poland’s MSPO defense exhibition, the missile can intercept targets up to 10 kilometers away and 5 kilometers high.

Poland’s Special Services Chief Meets CIA Director Amid Fears of Russian Threat to NATO — Poland’s special services minister Tomasz Siemoniak met CIA Director John Ratcliffe near Washington to discuss Poland’s security amid growing concerns over Russia’s potential threat to NATO. The meeting followed Ratcliffe’s recent talks with senior Russian officials and renewed US diplomatic efforts involving Ukraine, Russia, and NATO security.

West Braces for Ukraine War to Stretch Into 2027 as Putin Rejects Peace Push — US and European officials increasingly expect Russia’s war against Ukraine to continue into 2027 after the latest push to revive peace talks with the Kremlin failed to produce a breakthrough. Moscow is instead preparing for intensified attacks on Ukraine’s energy infrastructure as winter approaches.

How Russia Is Trying to Paralyze Kyiv Without Occupying It — Russia has shifted from concentrated nighttime barrages to near-continuous strikes using faster jet-powered drones. The campaign is designed to exhaust air defenses, disrupt work and transit, damage commercial logistics, and exert sustained psychological pressure on a capital Moscow failed to capture.

Russia’s New Jet Drones With Chinese Engines Challenge Ukraine’s Defenses — Russia is expanding its use of jet-powered attack drones fitted with Chinese-made engines, forcing Ukraine to adapt its air defenses as interception rates fall.

What Ramstein Revealed: 300 Patriots, a $27 Billion Gap and Russia’s Longer War — The 36th Ukraine Defense Contact Group exposed Kyiv’s immediate need for 300 Patriot interceptors, a $27 billion defense funding gap and growing concern that Russia is preparing for a longer war.

Rutte: Civilian Deaths in Ukraine Highest Since May 2022 as Aid Delays Cost Lives — Mark Rutte said civilian deaths in Ukraine are at their highest since May 2022, urging allies to boost support despite $10 billion already committed through PURL and US military sales.

US Destroys Five Iranian Oil Tankers as Tehran Threatens Vessels Off Kuwait, Bahrain — US forces destroyed five Iranian oil tankers on Tuesday in retaliation for attempted Iranian ballistic missile strikes on an American warship, as Tehran responded by warning tanker crews near Kuwait and Bahrain to abandon their vessels.

Zelensky, Støre Discuss Air Defense, FREYJA and Winter Aid Ahead of Royal Funeral — President Volodymyr Zelensky met Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre in Oslo for talks on air defense, interceptor missiles, the FREYJA program, and preparations for winter ahead of King Harald V’s funeral.

Hungary Blocks Ukraine's EU Accession Clusters for Fourth Time, Withholds Its Demands — Hungary blocked the opening of EU accession clusters 2 and 3 for Ukraine for a fourth time on Tuesday, Sept. 8, according to sources, who also said that Budapest refused to disclose which legislative steps regarding the minority issue it expects Kyiv to take.

Trump, Putin Discuss Ukraine in Hour-Long ‘Extremely Frank’ Call — The Kremlin announced that Russian President Vladimir Putin held an hour-long call with US President Donald Trump on Tuesday, Sept. 8, focused on ending the war. The call came hours after the death toll in overnight Russian strikes on Kyiv rose to five, following a visit by US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner to both Moscow and Kyiv as part of a broader effort to revive stalled diplomacy and broker an end to the war.

Ukraine Signs Contracts for 1,000 Patriot Missiles as Germany Pledges Interceptors From Its Own Reserves — Ahead of the 36th meeting of the Ukraine Defense Contact Group (the Ramstein format), which took place in the form of a video conference on Tuesday, Sept. 8, German Defense Minister Boris Pistorius said Germany would deliver the PAC-2 missiles to Ukraine from its own Bundeswehr stocks. Separately, Ukraine’s Defense Minister Yevhen Khmara announced contracts are being signed with partners fo

Russian Strikes Kill 2 in Dnipropetrovsk, Wound Over a Dozen Across Kharkiv, Chernihiv Regions — Russian strikes killed two people and wounded 13 others across three regions on Tuesday, Sept. 8. The Dnipropetrovsk region bore the brunt of the attack, having been hit nearly 50 times with drones, artillery, and an aerial bomb (KAB), according to regional authorities.

Ukraine Extends Full Tuition Compensation for Veterans' Children — Ukraine’s government has extended a program covering full tuition cost for veterans’ children in the 2026-27 academic year. According to Prime Minister Serhii Koretskyi on Tuesday, Sept. 8, students must confirm a certificate in the Diia app within 20 calendar days to receive the funds.

EU Clears €3.2B Patriot Purchase for Ukraine Under €90B Loan — EU member states agreed to allow Ukraine to use €3.2 billion from a €90 billion support loan to purchase Patriot interceptors. The decision is expected to be finalized by Sept. 11.

Russian Generals Simulate War With NATO for Years — Russia’s senior military leadership has used computer simulations to rehearse hypothetical wars with NATO and its partners since at least 2017, according to a Dossier Center investigation. The exercises involved scenarios around Sweden’s Gotland island, Japan and US forces. Before invading Ukraine, Russian commanders held such games monthly, but investigators say the simulations failed to anticipate Moscow’s battlefield problems.

Moscow Used US Envoys to Deliver Tougher Peace Demands — Ukrainian parliamentarian Anna Skorokhod says the Witkoff-Kushner mission failed, with Russia presenting Kyiv harsher peace terms. Ukrainian media reported continued deadlock, while Russian media showed Witkoff and Kushner smiling under a Russian wartime propaganda sign.

Ukraine Unveils Koral Air Defense Missile Launcher for First Time — Ukraine presented the self-propelled launcher for its Koral surface-to-air missile at Poland’s MSPO defense exhibition. The 450-kilogram missile carries a 36-kilogram warhead and uses inertial navigation, radio correction and active radar homing.

‘I’m Not Soviet Armenia’s Communist Party Chief’ – Pashinyan Pushes Back on Moscow — Pashinyan mocked suggestions that Moscow had “summoned” him or could force Armenia to hold a referendum on choosing between the EU and the Russia-led EAEU. His response follows Armenia’s suspension of participation in Moscow’s military alliance, deepening ties with Europe and the US, resistance to Russian economic pressure and a decisive electoral defeat for pro-Russian parties.

Ukraine Is Facing Another Financing Crisis — Trump has floated demanding repayment for US support to Ukraine, claiming over $300 billion – a figure far exceeding Kiel Institute’s tracked $133 billion. With US aid at zero since 2025, Europe already shoulders most funding, while Ukraine faces a $27-32 billion financing gap this year. Ukraine is meanwhile already facing financial strain. Seizing immobilized Russian central bank assets remains the cleanest fix, but political will is lacking.

Russia Says It Expects Ukraine Peace Talks to Resume as Deadly Attack Hits Kyiv — Russia says it expects trilateral talks with Ukraine and the US to resume, even as its forces launched a deadly attack on Kyiv. Peskov also welcomed US and Indian peace efforts and accused Kyiv of prolonging the war.

Zelensky Offers Presidential Plane for Witkoff and Kushner’s Next Kyiv Visit — President Volodymyr Zelensky offered to send Ukraine’s presidential plane to Poland or varying countries to bring Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner to Kyiv for their visit.

Hungary Expels 10 Russian Mission Staff for ‘Unacceptable Activities’ — Hungary is expelling 10 Russian diplomats over alleged activities deemed unacceptable under the Vienna Convention, in a major shift from Budapest’s traditionally close ties with Moscow. Russia vowed a “harsh and painful” response.

Zelensky Reveals Possible Venues for Trilateral Talks — Ukraine is seeking renewed trilateral talks with the US and Russia, with the UAE, Switzerland, and Turkey under consideration as venues. President Volodymyr Zelensky said prisoner exchanges, energy, and grain exports should top the agenda and insisted Europe participate in all future formats.

Ukraine Names Hanna Hvozdiar Deputy Defense Minister to Scale Arms Production — Ukraine's Cabinet of Ministers appointed Hanna Hvozdiar as deputy defense minister on Sept. 8, tasking her with scaling up weapons production and exports as Kyiv arms its front lines faster.

Russia Turns Back to US Chips in Kinzhal Missiles After Trying to Replace Them With Domestic Parts — Russia replaced US-made processors in Kinzhal missiles with domestic chips in 2023, but newer missiles again use American processors. Vlasyuk says foreign electronics remain critical to Russia’s weapons industry, with components made in 2025 and 2026 still appearing in Russian systems.

Russia Starts Blocking Reservists From Leaving Country — A 24-year-old Russian reservist was barred from traveling abroad after a military enlistment office imposed an exit restriction, in what activists described as the first known such case. The man only discovered the ban at passport control. Rights advocates cautioned that the incident does not prove Russia has introduced restrictions for all reservists.

‘God Willing, There Will Be a Result’: Zelensky Expects Trump Meeting in September — Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky expects to meet Donald Trump in the second half of September and plans to press the US president for ballistic missiles and support for Ukraine’s “Freya” missile program as Kyiv seeks to revive stalled peace talks.

FSB Detains Moldovan Accused of Attempted Murder of Russian General — Russian authorities say they have detained a 21-year-old Moldovan in the Astrakhan region suspected of the Sept. 3 attempted murder of a Russian general in the Saratov region on behalf of Ukraine.

Russian Drone Strike Injures 5 at TV Channel During Live Broadcast — A Russian strike drone hit the “We Are Ukraine “TV channel building during a live broadcast, President Zelensky has reported. Five people were injured, for which he called for a strong international response.

UK Sends Patriot Missiles as Russia Prepares to Turn Winter Into a Weapon — Britain will provide Ukraine with a £100 million military aid package through NATO’s PURL mechanism. Patriot missiles and other air defense equipment are expected to arrive before the winter season.

Two Russian Su-35S Fighters Collide Over Kursk Region — On Monday, three Russian milbloggers reported the loss of two Su-35S fighter aircraft and a pilot while flying combat missions over the Kursk region, the cause of which has yet to be confirmed.

Ukraine Hits Saratov Refinery Again as Russian Fuel Crisis Deepens — Ukrainian drones struck Saratov overnight, reportedly targeting the Rosneft oil refinery for the fourth time this year. The attack injured 10 people, including three children, as Kyiv intensifies strikes on Russia’s oil infrastructure amid a deepening fuel crisis.

Russian Shaheds Target Kyiv to Sumy Train — Two Russian Shahed drones carried out targeted strikes against a Kyiv-Sumy passenger train near Sumy, Ukrzaliznytsia said. The railway’s monitoring team stopped the train before the attack, allowing all passengers and crew members to evacuate safely. Buses were provided to take travelers to their destinations, and no injuries were reported.

175 Targets Down, But Ballistic Missiles Still Get Through — Ukraine intercepted 175 Russian aerial targets overnight, but Zelensky said ballistic missiles remain a major air-defense challenge. The attack also appeared to end Russia’s three-day pause on strikes against Kyiv before its stated deadline.

Satellite Images Reveal What Ukrainian Drones Hit at Russian Airbase Near the Border — Ukrainian drones reportedly struck Russia’s Taganrog-Tsentralny airbase overnight on Sept. 7, destroying a Mi-8 helicopter and damaging a Mi-35, according to OSINT analysts.
CARTOON: Game Over! — Serhii Kolyada’s ironic take on the latest international events.

‘Unpredictable Times’: Finland Fortifies NATO Frontier with 200-km Russia Border Fence — Finland has completed a €356 million, 200-kilometer security fence along vulnerable sections of its 1,340-kilometer border with Russia. Built after Russia’s invasion of Ukraine, the barrier includes surveillance systems and patrol infrastructure. Finland says the border crossings will remain closed due to ongoing security threats and alleged Russian hybrid operations, reflecting its strengthened NATO-era def

NATO Scrambled Fighter Jets Nearly 700 Times in Two Years Over Russian Air Provocations — NATO scrambled fighter jets nearly 700 times in two years to intercept Russian aircraft near Alliance airspace, its top military official said, warning that threats from Moscow extend beyond conventional warfare.

France, Italy Working on SAMP/T Delivery as Allies Explore More Patriot Systems for Ukraine — France and Italy are working to deliver Ukraine a SAMP/T air defense system and Aster missiles, while countries operating Patriot systems are exploring ways to rapidly send additional units to Kyiv ahead of winter.

Just How Likely Is Le Pen to Win? — Marine Le Pen enters the 2027 race with a broader electorate and a weaker anti-far-right opposition than in her previous campaigns. Her victory is not inevitable, but France's divided center and left have yet to produce a rival capable of stopping her.

What to Make of Witkoff and Kushner’s Return to Russia-Ukraine Peace Talks — Overall, the talks in Moscow and Kyiv represented a soft reset of the negotiating process. In both visits, Witkoff and Kushner discussed peace and economic proposals, exploring how to get the negotiations back on track. Neither set of meetings produced any real breakthroughs.
ISW Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment, September 7, 2026 — War in Ukraine - Latest update, key takeaways and map from the Institute for the Study of War on September 7, 2026.

Russia Pounds Kyiv With Missiles and Drones, Killing 5, Injuring 35 as US Envoys Leave — Russia launched a deadly missile and drone attack on Kyiv as US envoys departed, killing 5, injuring 35 and trapping residents.

Russia Appears to Break Its Own Three-Day Kyiv Truce Before Deadline — Russian drone activity over Kyiv before Moscow’s stated deadline suggested the Kremlin failed to observe even its limited three-day truce.

Ukraine’s Prosecutor General Kravchenko Resigns Over Corruption Accusations — Ruslan Kravchenko submitted his resignation after President Volodymyr Zelensky met with him over his future and days after anti-corruption investigators searched premises used by the prosecutor general.

Burnham, Trump Agree to Keep Working Toward Ukraine-Russia Ceasefire — British Prime Minister Andy Burnham and US President Donald Trump agreed to continue efforts toward a ceasefire after US envoys held back-to-back talks with Vladimir Putin and Volodymyr Zelensky.

TITLE: Греки та серби найрідше перевіряють інформацію з інтернету: статистика | LEDE:

У середньому 29,2% жителів країн Євросоюзу перевіряють у різних джерелах правдивість інформації з інтернету. Про це свідчать дані Євростату за 2025 рік. Статистика охоплює людей у віці від 16 до 74
